# Simulations

## Slido

## Understanding cause is hard

## What are simulations?

<!-- Animate this! --> 

- We create our own imaginary world
- In our imaginary world, we get to create our own rules
- Then we can observe what happens to our world when it follows our own rules
- Because we create our own rules, we know that what happens to our world is purely caused by 1. Our own rules and 2. The laws of probability.

## Purpose of simulations {.center}

Statistics asks:
- Based on what we observe in our imaginary world, what are the laws of probability?
- If you observe my world without knowing my rules, can you use probability to guess my rules?

## {.center}

::: {.card-list-center .non-incremental}

- Let's build our own simulation

:::

# Building a simulation: height $\rightarrow$ CLT

## Height $\rightarrow$ CLT {.center}

::: {.card-list-center .non-incremental}

- We will be using a simulation of height to derive a key law in statistics: the Central Limit Theorem (CLT)

:::

## First, a puzzle
- Puzzle: why are there are so many normally distributed data in the world?
- Even in vastly different areas, the normal distribution shows up a lot.
- Is there a shared process that can explain them all?

<!-- Show some real plots of height, psychological variables, gif of balls dropping etc. -->

- Answer: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT)

## Central Limit Theorem (CLT): Basic idea
- Explains how data can become normally distributed

<!-- animation of CLT in action -->

# Building a simulation: the details of height

## First, let's think mechanism
- What are some factors that cause differences in height?
    - Try to think of direct causes, not just correlation.

<!-- draw dags --> 

## Impact of these factors
- How much do these factors impact height?
    - At a maximum, how many inches do these factors add or subtract?
    - Remember, we are creating an imaginary world, so it doesn't have to be accurate!

## Building the simulation structure
I propose, that in my imaginary world, this is the "truth" of how height is constructed:

<!-- draw this all out 

- There's an average height
- Then, for each person, we sample some values for all the factors
- The final height for a person is the sum of the average height and their sampled factor values.

- For each person, we do the following: 
- There's an average height
- Then, for each factor, we sample some values
- We add the average height and the factor values together
- This is our final height for this person
- We repeat for 100 people
- At the end, we have a list of heights for 100 people


-->

<div id="hp">
  <div class="layout">
    <div>
      <div class="col-label">Steps — drag to reorder, drop words onto blanks</div>
      <div class="step-fixed">
        <span class="step-num">1.</span>
        <span>simulated_heights = empty_list</span>
        <span style="margin-left:8px;font-size:10px;color:#aaa;">(given)</span>
      </div>
      <div id="step-list"></div>
    </div>
    <div>
      <div class="col-label">Word Bank</div>
      <div id="word-bank"></div>
      <div class="tip">Drag onto a blank, or click a filled blank to remove it.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="actions" id="actions"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function () {

  const ITEMS = [
    { id: 'repeat_start',   parts: ['start repeat: for each person out of 100 people, do the following:'], blanks: [], answers: [] },
    { id: 'genetics',       parts: ['genetics = ', null],                                                   blanks: [null], answers: ['sample_between(-4, 4)'] },
    { id: 'nutrition',      parts: ['nutrition = ', null],                                                  blanks: [null], answers: ['sample_between(-3, 3)'] },
    { id: 'exercise',       parts: ['exercise = ', null],                                                   blanks: [null], answers: ['sample_between(-2, 2)'] },
    { id: 'final_height',   parts: ['final_height = ', null, ' + ', null, ' + ', null, ' + ', null],        blanks: [null, null, null, null], answers: ['average_height', 'genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise'] },
    { id: 'average_height', parts: ['average_height = ', null],                                             blanks: [null], answers: ['66'] },
    { id: 'add_to_list',    parts: ['simulated_heights = ', null],                                          blanks: [null], answers: ['add_to_list(final_height)'] },
    { id: 'repeat_end',     parts: ['end repeat'],                                                          blanks: [], answers: [] },
  ];

  const CORRECT_ORDER = ['repeat_start','genetics','nutrition','exercise','final_height','average_height','add_to_list','repeat_end'];

  const WORD_BANK_WORDS = ['66','sample_between(-2, 2)','sample_between(-3, 3)','sample_between(-4, 4)','average_height','genetics','nutrition','exercise','add_to_list(final_height)'];

  let order = shuffle(ITEMS.map(i => ({ ...i, blanks: [...i.blanks] })));
  let checked = false;
  let feedbackShown = false;
  let lastMsg = '';
  let lastMsgClass = '';

  let dragSrcStep = null;
  let dragWbWord = null;
  let dragSlotRef = null;

  function shuffle(arr) {
    for (let i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
      const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
      [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]];
    }
    return arr;
  }

  function getUsedWords() {
    const used = {};
    order.forEach(item => item.blanks.forEach(v => { if (v) used[v] = (used[v] || 0) + 1; }));
    return used;
  }

function validateOrder() {
    const ids = order.map(o => o.id);
    const idx = id => ids.indexOf(id);

    // repeat_start must be before repeat_end
    if (idx('repeat_start') >= idx('repeat_end')) return false;

    // genetics, nutrition, exercise must all be inside the loop (after repeat_start, before repeat_end)
    for (const id of ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']) {
      if (idx(id) <= idx('repeat_start') || idx(id) >= idx('repeat_end')) return false;
    }

    // final_height must be inside the loop, after genetics, nutrition, and exercise
    if (idx('final_height') <= idx('repeat_start') || idx('final_height') >= idx('repeat_end')) return false;
    for (const id of ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']) {
      if (idx('final_height') <= idx(id)) return false;
    }

    // add_to_list must be inside the loop, after final_height
    if (idx('add_to_list') <= idx('final_height') || idx('add_to_list') >= idx('repeat_end')) return false;

    // average_height can be anywhere before final_height (inside or outside loop)
    if (idx('average_height') >= idx('final_height')) return false;

    return true;
  }

  function validateBlanks() {
    const SAMPLES = ['sample_between(-2, 2)', 'sample_between(-3, 3)', 'sample_between(-4, 4)'];

    for (const item of order) {
      if (item.id === 'genetics' || item.id === 'nutrition' || item.id === 'exercise') {
        // Any of the three sample values is acceptable
        if (!SAMPLES.includes(item.blanks[0])) return false;
        // But each must be unique — no two can share the same sample value
      }
      if (item.id === 'average_height') {
        if (item.blanks[0] !== '66') return false;
      }
      if (item.id === 'final_height') {
        // Must be average_height + the three ids assigned to genetics/nutrition/exercise, in any order
        const gne = ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise'];
        const expected = new Set(['average_height', ...gne]);
        const given = new Set(item.blanks.filter(Boolean));
        if (![...expected].every(v => given.has(v))) return false;
        if (![...given].every(v => expected.has(v))) return false;
      }
      if (item.id === 'add_to_list') {
        if (item.blanks[0] !== 'add_to_list(final_height)') return false;
      }
    }

    // Each sample value must be used exactly once across genetics/nutrition/exercise
    const samplesUsed = ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']
      .map(id => order.find(o => o.id === id).blanks[0])
      .filter(Boolean);
    if (new Set(samplesUsed).size !== samplesUsed.length) return false;

    return true;
  }

  function allCorrect() {
    return validateOrder() && validateBlanks();
  }

  function render() {
    renderSteps();
    renderWordBank();
    renderActions();
  }

  function renderSteps() {
    const list = document.getElementById('step-list');
    list.innerHTML = '';

    order.forEach((item, stepIdx) => {
      const div = document.createElement('div');
      div.className = 'step';
      div.draggable = true;

      div.addEventListener('dragstart', e => {
        if (dragWbWord !== null || dragSlotRef !== null) { e.preventDefault(); return; }
        dragSrcStep = stepIdx;
        e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
        setTimeout(() => div.classList.add('dragging'), 0);
      });
      div.addEventListener('dragend', () => { div.classList.remove('dragging'); dragSrcStep = null; });
      div.addEventListener('dragover', e => {
        e.preventDefault();
        if (dragSrcStep !== null && dragSrcStep !== stepIdx) div.classList.add('drag-over');
      });
      div.addEventListener('dragleave', () => div.classList.remove('drag-over'));
      div.addEventListener('drop', e => {
        e.preventDefault();
        div.classList.remove('drag-over');
        if (dragSrcStep !== null && dragSrcStep !== stepIdx) {
          const moved = order.splice(dragSrcStep, 1)[0];
          order.splice(stepIdx, 0, moved);
          dragSrcStep = null;
          render();
        }
      });

      const handle = document.createElement('span');
      handle.className = 'drag-handle';
      handle.textContent = '⠿';
      div.appendChild(handle);

      const num = document.createElement('span');
      num.className = 'step-num';
      num.textContent = (stepIdx + 2) + '.';
      div.appendChild(num);

      let blankIdx = 0;
      item.parts.forEach(part => {
        if (part === null) {
          const bi = blankIdx++;
          const slot = document.createElement('span');
          const isFilled = !!item.blanks[bi];
          slot.className = 'slot' + (isFilled ? ' filled' : '');

          slot.textContent = item.blanks[bi] || '?';

          slot.addEventListener('dragover', e => {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            if (dragWbWord !== null || dragSlotRef !== null) slot.classList.add('drag-target');
          });
          slot.addEventListener('dragleave', () => slot.classList.remove('drag-target'));
          slot.addEventListener('drop', e => {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            slot.classList.remove('drag-target');
            if (dragWbWord !== null) {
              item.blanks[bi] = dragWbWord;
              dragWbWord = null;
              render();
            } else if (dragSlotRef !== null && !(dragSlotRef.itemId === item.id && dragSlotRef.blankIdx === bi)) {
              const srcItem = order.find(o => o.id === dragSlotRef.itemId);
              const srcVal = srcItem.blanks[dragSlotRef.blankIdx];
              srcItem.blanks[dragSlotRef.blankIdx] = item.blanks[bi];
              item.blanks[bi] = srcVal;
              dragSlotRef = null;
              render();
            }
          });

          if (isFilled) {
            slot.draggable = true;
            slot.addEventListener('dragstart', e => {
              dragSlotRef = { itemId: item.id, blankIdx: bi };
              dragWbWord = null;
              dragSrcStep = null;
              e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
              e.stopPropagation();
            });
            slot.addEventListener('dragend', () => { dragSlotRef = null; });
            slot.addEventListener('click', () => { item.blanks[bi] = null; render(); });
          }

          div.appendChild(slot);
        } else {
          const span = document.createElement('span');
          span.textContent = part;
          div.appendChild(span);
        }
      });

      list.appendChild(div);
    });
  }

  function renderWordBank() {
    const wb = document.getElementById('word-bank');
    wb.innerHTML = '';
    const used = getUsedWords();
    WORD_BANK_WORDS.forEach(word => {
      const span = document.createElement('span');
      span.className = 'wb-item' + (used[word] ? ' used' : '');
      span.textContent = word;
      span.draggable = !used[word];
      span.addEventListener('dragstart', e => {
        if (used[word]) { e.preventDefault(); return; }
        dragWbWord = word;
        dragSrcStep = null;
        e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'copy';
        setTimeout(() => span.classList.add('dragging-wb'), 0);
      });
      span.addEventListener('dragend', () => { span.classList.remove('dragging-wb'); dragWbWord = null; });
      wb.appendChild(span);
    });
  }

  function renderActions() {
    const actions = document.getElementById('actions');
    actions.innerHTML = '';

    const btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.className = 'btn-check';
    btn.textContent = checked ? 'Re-check' : 'Check answers';
    btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      checked = true;
      feedbackShown = true;
      if (allCorrect()) {
        lastMsg = '✓ All correct!';
        lastMsgClass = 'result ok';
      } else {
        // count mistakes
        const ids = order.map(o => o.id);
        const idx = id => ids.indexOf(id);
        const SAMPLES = ['sample_between(-2, 2)', 'sample_between(-3, 3)', 'sample_between(-4, 4)'];
        let mistakes = 0;
        if (idx('repeat_start') >= idx('repeat_end')) mistakes++;
        for (const id of ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise', 'final_height', 'add_to_list']) {
          if (idx(id) <= idx('repeat_start') || idx(id) >= idx('repeat_end')) mistakes++;
        }
        for (const id of ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']) {
          if (idx('final_height') <= idx(id)) mistakes++;
        }
        if (idx('add_to_list') <= idx('final_height')) mistakes++;
        if (idx('average_height') >= idx('final_height')) mistakes++;
        for (const id of ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']) {
          const val = order.find(o => o.id === id).blanks[0];
          if (!SAMPLES.includes(val)) mistakes++;
        }
        const samplesUsed = ['genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']
          .map(id => order.find(o => o.id === id).blanks[0]).filter(Boolean);
        if (new Set(samplesUsed).size !== samplesUsed.length) mistakes++;
        const fh = order.find(o => o.id === 'final_height').blanks;
        const expected = new Set(['average_height', 'genetics', 'nutrition', 'exercise']);
        const given = new Set(fh.filter(Boolean));
        if (![...expected].every(v => given.has(v)) || ![...given].every(v => expected.has(v))) mistakes++;
        if (order.find(o => o.id === 'average_height').blanks[0] !== '66') mistakes++;
        if (order.find(o => o.id === 'add_to_list').blanks[0] !== 'add_to_list(final_height)') mistakes++;
        lastMsg = `✗ ${mistakes} mistake${mistakes !== 1 ? 's' : ''} left`;
        lastMsgClass = 'result fail';
      }
      render();
      if (allCorrect()) {
        document.querySelectorAll('#hp .step').forEach(el => el.classList.add('correct'));
        document.querySelectorAll('#hp .slot.filled').forEach(el => el.classList.add('slot-correct'));
      } else {
        document.querySelectorAll('#hp .step').forEach(el => el.classList.add('incorrect'));
        document.querySelectorAll('#hp .slot').forEach(el => el.classList.add('slot-incorrect'));
      }
    });
    actions.appendChild(btn);

    if (feedbackShown) {
      const msg = document.createElement('span');
      msg.className = lastMsgClass;
      msg.textContent = lastMsg;
      actions.appendChild(msg);
      const reset = document.createElement('button');
      reset.className = 'btn-reset';
      reset.textContent = 'Reset';
      reset.addEventListener('click', () => {
        order = shuffle(ITEMS.map(i => ({ ...i, blanks: [...i.blanks] })));
        checked = false;
        feedbackShown = false;
        lastMsg = '';
        lastMsgClass = '';
        render();
      });
      actions.appendChild(reset);
    }
  }

  render();
})();
</script>

## Slido

What is the purpose of __?

## Importance of Central Limit Theorem (CLT)

- We will use the CLT in future classes to derive the Confidence Interval and p-values, which allows us to infer something about the real, "unknown rules" (more formally, the "population").


## Key takeaways

<!-- Or should I ask this as a question? -->

::: card-list
1. Simulations are imaginary worlds where we create our own rules
1. We can use simulations to derive laws in statistics; these laws used to infer the invisible rules
1. Height simulation: Many independent causes → normal distribution
:::
